metadata.title: An exact hypergeometric Weierstrass representation for Smyth's free-boundary minimal disk in the regular tetrahedron
metadata.abstract: Smyth (1984) proved that every tetrahedron $T\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ contains three embedded minimal disks meeting $\partial T$ orthogonally, obtained as conjugate surfaces of Plateau solutions in a skew quadrilateral $Q$ whose edges are $c_i\nu_i$, where $\varphi_1,\varphi_2,\varphi_3,\varphi_4$ are faces of $T$, $c_i=\operatorname{Area}(\varphi_i)$ and $\nu_i$ are outward normal vectors. For the $\textit{regular}$ tetrahedron we give the Weierstrass data explicitly. The Gauss map is a Schwarz triangle function for a circular-arc triangle with angles $(\pi/4,\ \pi/2,\ \pi\beta/2)$, where $\beta=\arccos(-1/3)/\pi$; the hypergeometric parameters are linear in $\beta$ and there is $\textit{no accessory parameter and no free parameter}$. We record a closed form for $\kappa$ in $\Gamma$-values, a Wronskian closed form for $g'$, the exact total curvature $2\pi(2\beta-1)$, the symmetric-square structure of the data, and a rigidity statement: since $\beta/2$ is irrational, the projective monodromy is dense and the data $\textit{cannot}$ be algebraic. Numerically the representation extends to 28 digits -- $\operatorname{Area}/\ell^{2}=0.2172341554075574483760009126\ldots$ -- confirming a 2013 Surface Evolver computation of Ken Brakke.
